messages:
alex: Heads-up — noticed the console's invoice preview jumps ~40% after a traffic spike is shadowed. Feels like the front-end estimator isn't smoothing sampled events right.

maya: Yeah saw that too on the demo org. The backend metering looks stable but the preview shows a large dip then spike. Could be sampling + window boundary.

kevin: @maya can you paste the console timeline? I want to check if the spike aligns with the routing change on Friday.

maya: Screenshot sent in thread, but quick summary: spike at 11:04, routing policy switched to fallback model group at 11:03:50 for ~90s. Metering ingest shows events at 11:04 but estimator preview smoothed them into the previous bucket.

sreena: Repro: I repro'd locally by replaying sampled events. The front-end estimator aggregates per-minute counts using an upsample factor from sampling rate metadata, but it uses the last-known sampling_rate for the whole minute. If sampling_rate changes mid-minute we overcorrect.

kevin: Ah. So if sampling drops (more sampling) mid-minute, we multiply earlier low-sampled counts by a too-large factor for the whole window -> big spike.

alex: Proposed UX fix: show a small badge "estimate smoothed" and display both raw ingested count and smoothed estimate, plus a tiny histogram of sampling-rate changes. That way users know when estimator heuristics caused the jump.

josh: Love the transparency idea. Also think we should fix heuristic: compute weighted upsample per sub-window instead of per-minute. Implementation: cut minute into 6 x 10s slices and apply sampling_rate per slice. Cheap and should reduce artifacts.

kevin: Implementation note: backend already emits sampling_rate change events to telemetry topic (metering.sampling_changes). We can consume those in the preview service to do slice-level estimation.

billing-bot: deploy:metering-preview-service v1.22 -> canary started on qa at 3295432120.

sreena: For rollout, can we make the console toggleable? default on for prod accounts after one-week canary. Also add a flag: `RENDER_ESTIMATE_SLICE_SIZE=10s` so ops can tune.

alex: Good. Who wants to own the console change and the preview-service change? I can do the console PR (small UI/tooltip + badge). @kevin take the preview service change?

kevin: I can pick preview-service. Plan: add subscription to metering.sampling_changes, build per-tenant in-memory sampling timeline keyed by minute -> compute slices on read, fall back to minute-level if data missing. Will add unit tests and a perf benchmark (target <5ms extra latency for preview).

maya: Also log a new metric `preview_estimate_delta` (abs(smoothed - previous_estimate)/previous_estimate) so we can alert if UX changes cause >20% swings for more than 5m.

josh: Can we also add small note in docs about quota windows and sampling artifacts? Customer support has a ticket that would have benefited from that explanation.

alex: Agreed. I'll file a docs ticket after I open the console PR.

kevin: I'll start the preview-service branch and ping infra for canary capacity. billing-bot, please annotate the canary when it's up.

billing-bot: canary:preview-service annotated on qa cluster at 3295432155 (tag: slice-estimate).

sreena: Quick checklist for rollout: 1) preview-service unit + perf tests 2) UI badge + tooltip 3) docs snippet 4) telemetry metric and alert 5) canary for 48h 6) prod flip. I'll add to the runbook.

alex: Perfect. Thanks everyone. If this reduces noisy invoice previews, should lower support churn. :thumbsup:
